_readme: MCP servers Coco starts. No secrets here: use "${env:NAME}" for tokens. Only tools listed under "tools" reach the model. Put personal additions in mcp_servers.local.json (git-ignored). See docs/mcp-setup.md.
_tool_groups: Servers listed in a group reach the model only once a conversation needs them: when a user message contains one of the keywords (whole words, any case) or matches one of the patterns (regular expressions; coding's matches owner/repo names like ggml-org/llama.cpp), or when the model calls load_tools. Then they stay for the rest of the conversation. Servers in no group are always loaded.

email.description: search and read the user's Gmail

github.description: the user's own GitHub account: their repositories, commits, issues and pull requests

coding.description: programming help: library documentation, Stack Overflow answers, and how open-source projects work

notes.description: Official MCP filesystem server, limited to the notes folder. Reviewed version, pinned.

list_directory.name: list_notes
list_directory.description: List all the files in the notes folder. Call this first whenever the user names a note by topic (e.g. 'my shopping list') instead of its exact file name.

read_text_file.name: read_file
read_text_file.description: Read the contents of a file in the notes folder. Needs the exact file name: never guess one. If the user didn't give it, call list_notes first and read the file that matches.

arg_descriptions.path: Just the file name inside the notes folder, e.g. 'todo.txt'. Do not include 'notes/'.

write_file.name: write_file
write_file.description: Write the contents to a file in the notes folder.

arg_descriptions.path: Just the file name inside the notes folder, e.g. 'todo.txt'. Do not include 'notes/'.
arg_descriptions.content: The exact literal text to save. Plain text only: no expressions, no string concatenation with +, no placeholders. If you need the current time, call current_time first and paste the result as plain text.

personal.description: Coco's own memory server (personal_server.py). Only touches the memory file.

remember.description: Save a lasting preference, fact, or decision about the user to long-term memory. Call this EVERY time the user says 'remember' or tells you something lasting about themselves. This tool is the only way anything gets saved: replying 'got it' or 'I'll remember' without calling it saves nothing.

arg_descriptions.fact: One short sentence restating what the user told you about themselves.
arg_descriptions.category: Preferences = how the user likes things done. Facts = things about the user. Decisions = choices the user made.

arg_descriptions.text: A distinctive part of the memory's text, copied from the memory shown in your prompt.

github.description: Official GitHub MCP server v2.1.0 (github/github-mcp-server release binary, unzipped into tools/). Read-only four ways: read-only token permissions, --read-only, --tools, and the allowlist below. Off by default: enable in mcp_servers.local.json once the token is set.
github._trimmed: Schemas cut from ~13,000 to a fraction of that (they load mid-conversation, so every token is re-read): pagination, sorting and field selectors hidden; list sizes and returned fields fixed by the host, which also makes results smaller.

get_me.name: github_whoami
get_me.description: Get the user's own GitHub login. It does not list repositories: use search_repositories with 'user:<login>' for that.

search_repositories.description: Search GitHub repositories. For the USER'S OWN repositories, call github_whoami first, then search 'user:<login>'. Without user: this searches all of GitHub.

arg_descriptions.query: GitHub search syntax, e.g. 'user:octocat' or 'machine learning language:python'.

get_file_contents.description: Read a file, or list a folder, in a GitHub repository.

arg_descriptions.path: File or folder path; '/' for the top folder.

list_commits.description: List the most recent commits of a GitHub repository (10, newest first).

arg_descriptions.path: Optional: only commits touching this file.
arg_descriptions.since: Optional: only commits after this date (YYYY-MM-DD).
arg_descriptions.until: Optional: only commits before this date (YYYY-MM-DD).

list_issues.description: List issues of a GitHub repository (10, open and closed unless state is given).

arg_descriptions.labels: Optional: only issues with these labels.

issue_read.description: Read one GitHub issue: its details, comments, sub-issues, parent or labels.

arg_descriptions.method: get = details; get_comments; get_sub_issues; get_parent; get_labels.

list_pull_requests.description: List pull requests of a GitHub repository (10).

pull_request_read.description: Read one GitHub pull request: details, diff, changed files, commits, comments, reviews or CI status.

arg_descriptions.method: get = details; get_diff; get_files; get_commits; get_comments (general); get_reviews; get_review_comments (code review threads); get_status / get_check_runs (CI).

gmail.description: Coco's own read-only Gmail server (gmail_server.py). Requests only the gmail.readonly scope; credentials live in %APPDATA%\coco, outside the repo. Off by default: enable in mcp_servers.local.json after running gmail_server.py --authorize.

web.description: Web search through a local SearXNG (Docker container coco-searxng on 127.0.0.1:8888, see docs/mcp-setup.md) via the mcp-searxng server. Free, no account or key. Pages are untrusted (prompt injection) and capped in size. web_url_read refuses private/internal addresses by default. Off by default: enable in mcp_servers.local.json once SearXNG is set up.

searxng_web_search.name: web_search
searxng_web_search.description: Search the web for current or general information that isn't in your memory or the user's notes/email: news, facts, prices, how-tos, docs. Returns titles, URLs and short snippets. Snippets are often enough to answer; read a page with read_web_page when they aren't. Snippets can be months old: for 'latest', 'current' or 'newest' questions, read the most official result (e.g. the project's own site) before answering.

arg_descriptions.query: Plain search keywords, like you'd type into a search engine.
arg_descriptions.time_range: Only for recent news: 'day', 'week', 'month' or 'year'. Leave out otherwise.

web_url_read.name: read_web_page
web_url_read.description: Open a web page (a search result, or a link the user gave) and return its text. Long pages are cut off.

arg_descriptions.url: The full http(s) URL of the page.

deepwiki.description: DeepWiki (Cognition), remote and free, no account: AI-written wikis of public GitHub repositories. Only ask_wiki_question is exposed; read_wiki_contents returns whole wikis, far too big for the context. Answers can take ~1 minute. Off by default.

ask_wiki_question.name: ask_repo_docs
ask_wiki_question.description: Ask how a PUBLIC open-source GitHub project works (its code, architecture, options), answered from DeepWiki's wiki of that repository. Not for the user's own repositories (use the GitHub tools) or general web questions. Can take up to a minute.

arg_descriptions.question: One specific question about that repository.

context7.description: Context7 (Upstash), remote and free: current documentation and code examples for programming libraries. Works without a key at a low hourly rate limit; a free key raises it (see docs/mcp-setup.md). Queries go to Context7, so never put private data in them. Off by default.

resolve-library-id.name: find_library
resolve-library-id.description: Step 1 for questions about using a programming library or framework (e.g. 'how do I stream with the openai Python SDK'): find its Context7 library id. Then call read_library_docs with that id.

arg_descriptions.libraryName: The library or framework name, e.g. 'next.js' or 'openai python'.
arg_descriptions.query: What the user wants to do with it, in a few words. No private data.

query-docs.name: read_library_docs
query-docs.description: Step 2: read current docs and code examples for a library id from find_library (format '/org/project').

arg_descriptions.libraryId: The exact library id from find_library, e.g. '/vercel/next.js'.
arg_descriptions.query: One specific topic to look up, e.g. 'streaming responses'. No private data.

stackoverflow.description: Coco's own read-only Stack Overflow server (stackoverflow_server.py) on the public Stack Exchange API. Free and keyless (~300 requests/day per IP); a free app key in STACKEXCHANGE_KEY raises it to 10,000 (see docs/mcp-setup.md). Off by default.

search_stackoverflow.description: Search Stack Overflow for a programming error message or coding problem. Returns question ids, titles, scores and whether they have an accepted answer. Then read the best one with read_stackoverflow_answers.
